item.title: Version 1.4.4
item.description: AI Assistant - Longer Memory — AI now remembers more of your conversation and project context - Smarter Context — More efficient use of tokens means better, more relevant responses - Project Awareness — Improved understanding of your codebase structure and files Code Editor - Full File Management — Right-click any file or folder to rename, duplicate, delete, copy path, or reveal in Finder - Create Files & Folders — Use the + button or right-click to create new Swift files, SwiftUI views, JSON, and more with smart templates - Drag & Drop — Move files between folders by dragging them directly in the sidebar - Beautiful Dialogs — Redesigned file creation sheets with visual file type selector Database Browser - Redesigned Data Viewer — Clean, full-width table layout inspired by modern database tools - Resizable Columns — Drag column edges to adjust widths to your preference - Type Badges — See column types (uuid, text, int4, timestamp) at a glance in headers - Enhanced Pagination — Jump to any page, choose rows per page (10, 25, 50, 100) - Row Selection — Select rows with checkboxes for future bulk operations - Improved Performance — Faster, smoother scrolling when browsing large tables General - Stability Improvements — Various fixes for smoother app performance - Better Error Handling — Clearer error messages when things go wrong

item.title: Version 2.3.2
item.description: - Enhanced mode - the new enhanced mode runs on Sonnet 4.6 with sharper code generation, better SwiftUI instincts, and faster multi-file operations. - Image Upload - Add images in the chat that the AI can use and input directly into your app.

item.title: Version 2.4.0
item.description: - Toolkit — Use #font, #color, #data, #sound, #lottie, #video, and #3d to drop assets straight into your app. Pick a file, tell the AI what you want, and it's automatically added, configured, and ready to use in your code. - Enhanced mode is now the default — Enhanced delivers stronger UI design, fewer mistakes, and deeper reasoning than Quick mode — at the same or lower cost. It's now the recommended mode for all projects. - Quick mode renamed — The old Standard mode is now called Quick, better reflecting what it's for: fast, lightweight iterations when you don't need full design power. - Smarter resource handling — Assets added through commands are now reliably bundled into your app build. Fixed an issue where fonts, audio, data files, and other resources could silently fail to register.
